# Recover the editable agreement

The procurement team has the published PDF of its facilities monitoring
agreement but has lost the editable Word file. Reconstruct it for the next
contract revision.

Read `/app/BRIEF.md` and reconstruct `/app/input/agreement.pdf` as
`/app/submission/agreement.docx`. Also deliver a reproducible script at
`/app/submission/rebuild.py` (and any local assets it needs) and a concise
`/app/submission/verification.md` describing what you checked and any limitations.

The Word document is the principal deliverable. Preserve the agreement's
meaning and visual organization while making its ordinary text, clauses and
tables genuinely editable. A PDF pasted into Word as page images is not a
reconstruction.

Python-docx, PyMuPDF, Pillow, LibreOffice Writer and Liberation/DejaVu fonts
are installed. You may inspect and render the PDF and your document, write
helpers and run local checks. No outside source data or conversion service
is needed. Preserve `/app/input` and `/app/BRIEF.md`.

Evaluation uses a fixed LLM document-quality rubric against the hidden
original Word source, not your conversation or tool-use trajectory. The
rubric, weights and acceptance thresholds are in the brief.

# Editorial and acceptance brief

## Deliverable

Recreate the supplied fictional agreement as a useful editable DOCX. The PDF
is authoritative for all content, figures, labels, numerical values and
relationships. No external legal knowledge is required. Do not add terms.

Keep the same major sections, reading order, table relationships, captions,
headers/footers, footnote associations and signature fields. Preserve the
distinction between contractual text, explanatory notes and document furniture.
Retain visible clause numbers and cross-reference targets.

## Editability

Use real Word paragraphs and heading styles. Use automatic Word numbering
for the numbered clauses, real tables for schedules/pricing/signatures and
real footnotes for footnotes. Table headers should repeat if a table flows
to another page. Numbered clauses must remain renumberable; cross-reference
text must continue to identify the intended clause in the delivered version.
Live cross-reference fields are welcome but are not mandatory.

Keep figures as separate images or drawing objects with editable captions;
their internal artwork need not be editable. Do not turn entire pages,
paragraphs or tables into images. Avoid one text box per line or word: the
body must reflow when a paragraph grows. Working headings and tables matter
more than mimicking the original's private style names or XML.

## Visual fidelity

Preserve the hierarchy, columns, portrait/landscape orientation where used,
table groupings, major page/section breaks and figure proportions. Use
available fonts with similar metrics. Modest font, spacing or pagination
differences are acceptable. Exact pixels, line breaks, ZIP bytes, style IDs
and the original internal XML are not required.

No omitted text, incorrect amount, swapped table association, unreadable
glyph, material overlap or clipped row is acceptable. A small pagination
shift is preferable to clipping content to force an exact page count.

## Rebuild and check

`python /app/submission/rebuild.py` must recreate `agreement.docx` from the
PDF and any delivered local code/assets without network access. Keep any
generated intermediates outside `/app/submission`. Your script may contain
manually reconstructed text/layout; a general-purpose PDF converter is not
required. Do not merely store a finished DOCX under another name and copy it.

Check your rendered output and describe remaining limitations honestly.
After copying your document, the verifier extends one body clause and a
table description and renders the edited copy. It assesses whether these
ordinary edits still produce usable text and a table, not exact edited
pagination. These probes do not modify your submitted original.

## LLM grading

The judge is GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`), high reasoning, through Copilot CLI
1.0.102. It receives reference/candidate page renders, extracted text and
Word structure, and edited-copy evidence. It does not receive the agent
trajectory or score the verification note's claims as proof.

The judge scores each dimension from 0 to 4:

* Content fidelity, 35%: words, numbers, symbols, conditions and associations.
* Editable structure, 30%: headings, paragraphs, numbering, tables, footnotes
  and edit/reflow behavior.
* Visual organization, 25%: layout, hierarchy, tables, figures and legibility.
* Navigation and document furniture, 10%: headings, clause references,
  headers/footers, captions and note placement.

Anchors: 4 = faithful and usable, only negligible differences; 3 = minor
localized defects without material loss; 2 = substantial repair needed;
1 = severe losses or largely unusable; 0 = absent or fundamentally wrong.
Each score must cite document evidence. The weighted score is divided by 4.
Acceptance requires at least 0.85 overall and at least 3 in every dimension.
A score of 3 means minor defects, not permission for an incorrect financial
amount or omitted contractual obligation.

Two independent judge calls use the same evidence and rubric. Scores are
averaged. A third call is made if the first two disagree on acceptance or
differ by at least two points in any dimension; the median per dimension
then determines the result. All calls and the disagreement are preserved.
Model/API/rendering errors are infrastructure errors, not candidate failures.

Basic artifact checks also require a readable DOCX, protected inputs,
required deliverables and a successful offline rebuild/render. A failure
claim must be backed by a concrete document defect, not by a score alone.
The rebuild has a 180-second limit in the provided four-CPU environment;
this is a reconstruction script, not a new agent run.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rebuild /app/submission/agreement.docx from the issued PDF.

The text, tables and layout below were reconstructed manually from
/app/input/agreement.pdf.  The two figure images are extracted from that
PDF at build time (PyMuPDF); everything else is native Word content:
styles, automatic clause numbering, real tables, a real footnote,
sections (two-column and landscape), header/footer and fields.

Usage:  python /app/submission/rebuild.py [output.docx]
"""
import copy
import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import fitz  # PyMuPDF
from docx import Document
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT, WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT
from docx.opc.constants import RELATIONSHIP_TYPE as RT
from docx.opc.packuri import PackURI
from docx.opc.part import Part
from docx.oxml import parse_xml
from docx.oxml.ns import nsdecls, qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor, Emu

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PDF = Path("/app/input/agreement.pdf")
OUT = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else HERE / "agreement.docx"

BODY_FONT = "Liberation Sans"
HEAD_FONT = "DejaVu Sans"
NAVY = RGBColor(0x17, 0x3B, 0x55)
ACCENT = RGBColor(0x4F, 0x81, 0xBD)
MARGIN_LR = Inches(0.72)
TABLE_STYLE = "Light Shading Accent 1"

CLAUSE_NUM_ID = 90
_bookmark_id = [100]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def set_fonts(rpr_owner_font, name):
    """Set explicit font on a style/run font, dropping theme-font overrides."""
    rPr = rpr_owner_font.element.get_or_add_rPr() if hasattr(rpr_owner_font, "element") else None
    return rPr


def style_font(style, name=None, size=None, bold=None, italic=None, color=None):
    rPr = style.element.get_or_add_rPr()
    if name:
        old = rPr.find(qn("w:rFonts"))
        if old is not None:
            rPr.remove(old)
        rf = OxmlElement("w:rFonts")
        for a in ("w:ascii", "w:hAnsi", "w:cs", "w:eastAsia"):
            rf.set(qn(a), name)
        rPr.insert(0, rf)
    if color is not None:
        old = rPr.find(qn("w:color"))
        if old is not None:
            rPr.remove(old)
        style.font.color.rgb = color
    f = style.font
    if size is not None:
        f.size = Pt(size)
    if bold is not None:
        f.bold = bold
    if italic is not None:
        f.italic = italic


def para_fmt(style, before=None, after=None, line=None, keep_next=None):
    pf = style.paragraph_format
    if before is not None:
        pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if after is not None:
        pf.space_after = Pt(after)
    if line is not None:
        pf.line_spacing = line
    if keep_next is not None:
        pf.keep_with_next = keep_next


def add_bookmark(paragraph, name):
    bid = str(_bookmark_id[0])
    _bookmark_id[0] += 1
    start = parse_xml(f'<w:bookmarkStart {nsdecls("w")} w:id="{bid}" w:name="{name}"/>')
    end = parse_xml(f'<w:bookmarkEnd {nsdecls("w")} w:id="{bid}"/>')
    p = paragraph._p
    pPr = p.find(qn("w:pPr"))
    if pPr is not None:
        pPr.addnext(start)
    else:
        p.insert(0, start)
    p.append(end)


def _run_xml(text, rpr=""):
    t = text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")
    return f'<w:r {nsdecls("w")}>{rpr}<w:t xml:space="preserve">{t}</w:t></w:r>'


def add_field(paragraph, instr, result, rpr=""):
    """Append a complex field (begin/instr/separate/result/end)."""
    p = paragraph._p
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {nsdecls("w")}>{rpr}<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"/></w:r>'))
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {nsdecls("w")}>{rpr}<w:instrText xml:space="preserve"> {instr} </w:instrText></w:r>'))
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {nsdecls("w")}>{rpr}<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="separate"/></w:r>'))
    p.append(parse_xml(_run_xml(result, rpr)))
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {nsdecls("w")}>{rpr}<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="end"/></w:r>'))


def add_link(paragraph, text, anchor):
    """Internal hyperlink to a bookmark, with ordinary text formatting."""
    h = parse_xml(f'<w:hyperlink {nsdecls("w")} w:anchor="{anchor}" w:history="1">{_run_xml(text)}</w:hyperlink>')
    paragraph._p.append(h)


def rich(paragraph, parts):
    """parts: str | ('b', text) | ('ref', bookmark, shown) | ('link', text, anchor)
    | ('pageref', bookmark, shown) | ('fn', id)."""
    for part in parts:
        if isinstance(part, str):
            paragraph.add_run(part)
        elif part[0] == "b":
            paragraph.add_run(part[1]).bold = True
        elif part[0] == "ref":
            add_field(paragraph, f"REF {part[1]} \\r \\h", part[2])
        elif part[0] == "pageref":
            add_field(paragraph, f"PAGEREF {part[1]} \\h", part[2])
        elif part[0] == "link":
            add_link(paragraph, part[1], part[2])
        elif part[0] == "fn":
            r = paragraph.add_run()
            r.style = "Footnote Reference"
            r._r.append(parse_xml(f'<w:footnoteReference {nsdecls("w")} w:id="{part[1]}"/>'))
    return paragraph


def set_cols(section, num, space_twips=720):
    sectPr = section._sectPr
    cols = sectPr.find(qn("w:cols"))
    if cols is None:
        cols = OxmlElement("w:cols")
        sectPr.append(cols)
    for a in list(cols.attrib):
        del cols.attrib[a]
    cols.set(qn("w:num"), str(num))
    cols.set(qn("w:space"), str(space_twips))


def page_setup(section, landscape=False):
    a4w, a4h = Emu(7560310), Emu(10692130)  # 210 x 297 mm
    if landscape:
        section.orientation = WD_ORIENT.LANDSCAPE
        section.page_width, section.page_height = a4h, a4w
    else:
        section.orientation = WD_ORIENT.PORTRAIT
        section.page_width, section.page_height = a4w, a4h
    section.left_margin = section.right_margin = MARGIN_LR
    section.top_margin = Inches(0.72)
    section.bottom_margin = Inches(0.72)
    section.header_distance = Inches(0.3)
    section.footer_distance = Inches(0.3)


def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    trPr.append(parse_xml(f'<w:tblHeader {nsdecls("w")}/>'))


def cant_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    trPr.append(parse_xml(f'<w:cantSplit {nsdecls("w")}/>'))


def make_table(doc, header, rows, widths=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1 + len(rows), cols=len(header))
    t.style = TABLE_STYLE
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    data = [header] + rows
    for r_i, row in enumerate(data):
        for c_i, val in enumerate(row):
            cell = t.cell(r_i, c_i)
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.style = "Table Text"
            if val:
                p.add_run(val)
    repeat_header(t.rows[0])
    for r in t.rows:
        cant_split(r)
    if widths:
        for c_i, w in enumerate(widths):
            for cell in t.columns[c_i].cells:
                cell.width = w
    return t


def body(doc, text_or_parts, style=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if isinstance(text_or_parts, str):
        p.add_run(text_or_parts)
    else:
        rich(p, text_or_parts)
    return p


def clause(doc, lead, parts, bookmark=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="Clause")
    rich(p, [("b", lead + " ")] + parts)
    if bookmark:
        add_bookmark(p, bookmark)
    return p


def h1(doc, text, bookmark, page_break=True):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(text, style="Heading 1")
    if page_break:
        p.paragraph_format.page_break_before = True
    add_bookmark(p, bookmark)
    return p


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- styles
def build_styles(doc):
    st = doc.styles
    normal = st["Normal"]
    style_font(normal, BODY_FONT, 10, color=RGBColor(0, 0, 0))
    para_fmt(normal, before=0, after=7, line=1.08)

    title = st["Title"]
    style_font(title, HEAD_FONT, 30, bold=False, color=NAVY)
    para_fmt(title, before=0, after=10, line=1.0)
    spacing = title.element.get_or_add_rPr().find(qn("w:spacing"))
    if spacing is not None:
        spacing.getparent().remove(spacing)

    sub = st["Subtitle"]
    style_font(sub, HEAD_FONT, 12, italic=True, color=ACCENT)
    para_fmt(sub, before=0, after=8, line=1.0)
    sp = sub.element.get_or_add_rPr().find(qn("w:spacing"))
    if sp is not None:
        sp.getparent().remove(sp)

    for name, size, before, after in (("Heading 1", 21, 18, 6), ("Heading 2", 13, 12, 6)):
        s = st[name]
        style_font(s, HEAD_FONT, size, bold=True, color=NAVY)
        para_fmt(s, before=before, after=after, line=1.0, keep_next=True)

    parties = st.add_style("Party Line", WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    parties.base_style = normal
    style_font(parties, HEAD_FONT, 13, bold=True, color=NAVY)
    para_fmt(parties, before=4, after=8, line=1.0, keep_next=True)

    cap = st["Caption"]
    style_font(cap, BODY_FONT, 9, bold=True, color=ACCENT)
    para_fmt(cap, before=0, after=10, line=1.08)

    tt = st.add_style("Table Text", WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    tt.base_style = normal
    tt.font.size = Pt(9)
    para_fmt(tt, before=2, after=3, line=1.08)

    cl = st.add_style("Clause", WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    cl.base_style = normal
    pPr = cl.element.get_or_add_pPr()
    pPr.append(parse_xml(f'<w:numPr {nsdecls("w")}><w:numId w:val="{CLAUSE_NUM_ID}"/></w:numPr>'))

    fig = st.add_style("Figure", WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    fig.base_style = normal
    fig.paragraph_format.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    para_fmt(fig, before=6, after=4, line=1.0, keep_next=True)

    fnt = st.add_style("Footnote Text", WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    fnt.base_style = normal
    para_fmt(fnt, before=0, after=0, line=1.08)
    fnr = st.add_style("Footnote Reference", WD_STYLE_TYPE.CHARACTER)
    fnr.font.superscript = True

    for name in ("Header", "Footer"):
        try:
            s = st[name]
        except KeyError:
            s = st.add_style(name, WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
            s.base_style = normal
        style_font(s, BODY_FONT, 8)
        para_fmt(s, before=0, after=0, line=1.0)


def build_numbering(doc):
    numbering = doc.part.numbering_part.element
    abstract = parse_xml(
        f'<w:abstractNum {nsdecls("w")} w:abstractNumId="{CLAUSE_NUM_ID}">'
        '<w:multiLevelType w:val="singleLevel"/>'
        '<w:lvl w:ilvl="0"><w:start w:val="1"/><w:numFmt w:val="decimal"/>'
        '<w:pStyle w:val="Clause"/>'
        '<w:lvlText w:val="%1."/><w:lvlJc w:val="left"/>'
        '<w:pPr><w:tabs><w:tab w:val="num" w:pos="360"/></w:tabs>'
        '<w:ind w:left="360" w:hanging="360"/></w:pPr></w:lvl></w:abstractNum>'
    )
    num = parse_xml(
        f'<w:num {nsdecls("w")} w:numId="{CLAUSE_NUM_ID}"><w:abstractNumId w:val="{CLAUSE_NUM_ID}"/></w:num>'
    )
    first_num = numbering.find(qn("w:num"))
    if first_num is not None:
        first_num.addprevious(abstract)
    else:
        numbering.append(abstract)
    numbering.append(num)


def build_footnotes(doc, notes):
    """notes: {id: [runs as parts]} -> real footnotes.xml part."""
    W = nsdecls("w")
    items = [
        f'<w:footnote w:type="separator" w:id="-1"><w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="240" w:lineRule="auto"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:separator/></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>',
        f'<w:footnote w:type="continuationSeparator" w:id="0"><w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="240" w:lineRule="auto"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:continuationSeparator/></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>',
    ]
    for fid, text in notes.items():
        t = text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<")
        items.append(
            f'<w:footnote w:id="{fid}"><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="FootnoteText"/></w:pPr>'
            f'<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="FootnoteReference"/></w:rPr><w:footnoteRef/></w:r>'
            f'<w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">{t}</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>'
        )
    xml = f'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n<w:footnotes {W}>' + "".join(items) + "</w:footnotes>"
    part = Part(
        PackURI("/word/footnotes.xml"),
        "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.footnotes+xml",
        xml.encode("utf-8"),
        doc.part.package,
    )
    doc.part.relate_to(part, RT.FOOTNOTES)
    # footnote properties in settings
    settings = doc.settings.element
    settings.append(parse_xml(
        f'<w:footnotePr {W}><w:footnote w:id="-1"/><w:footnote w:id="0"/></w:footnotePr>'))


def build_header_footer(section):
    hdr = section.header
    p = hdr.paragraphs[0]
    p.style = "Header"
    p.text = "MERIDIAN CIVIC ESTATES  /  PROCUREMENT SERVICES"

    ftr = section.footer
    p = ftr.paragraphs[0]
    p.style = "Footer"
    p.paragraph_format.tab_stops.clear_all()
    p.paragraph_format.tab_stops.add_tab_stop(Pt(186), WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT.LEFT)
    p.add_run("MCE-26-041  |  Issued 18 June 2026\tAgreement  /  ")
    add_field(p, "PAGE", "1", rpr='<w:rPr><w:sz w:val="20"/></w:rPr>')


def figure_images():
    """Extract the two figure bitmaps from the issued PDF (Schedule C page)."""
    d = fitz.open(PDF)
    page = d[5]
    infos = sorted(page.get_image_info(xrefs=True), key=lambda i: i["bbox"][1])
    out = []
    for info in infos:
        img = d.extract_image(info["xref"])
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = info["bbox"]
        out.append((io.BytesIO(img["image"]), (x1 - x0) / 72.0, (y1 - y0) / 72.0))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- content
def build():
    doc = Document()
    build_styles(doc)
    build_numbering(doc)
    build_footnotes(doc, {1: "Only complete 15-minute blocks after the included 45 minutes are "
                             "billable; 59 minutes incurs no additional block."})
    doc.core_properties.title = "Facilities monitoring and response agreement"
    doc.core_properties.subject = "Procurement reference MCE-26-041, Revision 2.1"
    doc.core_properties.author = "Meridian Civic Estates - Procurement Services"

    sec = doc.sections[0]

def add_bookmark(paragraph, name):
    bid = str(_bookmark_id[0])
    _bookmark_id[0] += 1
    start = parse_xml(f'<w:bookmarkStart {nsdecls("w")} w:id="{bid}" w:name="{name}"/>')
    end = parse_xml(f'<w:bookmarkEnd {nsdecls("w")} w:id="{bid}"/>')
    p = paragraph._p
    pPr = p.find(qn("w:pPr"))
    if pPr is not None:
        pPr.addnext(start)
    else:
        p.insert(0, start)
    p.append(end)


def _esc(text):
    return text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")


def _run_xml(text, rpr=""):
    return f'<w:r {nsdecls("w")}>{rpr}<w:t xml:space="preserve">{_esc(text)}</w:t></w:r>'


def add_field(paragraph, instr, result, rpr=""):
    """Append a complex field (begin / instr / separate / cached result / end)."""
    p = paragraph._p
    W = nsdecls("w")
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {W}>{rpr}<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="begin"/></w:r>'))
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {W}>{rpr}<w:instrText xml:space="preserve"> {instr} </w:instrText></w:r>'))
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {W}>{rpr}<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="separate"/></w:r>'))
    p.append(parse_xml(_run_xml(result, rpr)))
    p.append(parse_xml(f'<w:r {W}>{rpr}<w:fldChar w:fldCharType="end"/></w:r>'))


def add_link(paragraph, text, anchor):
    """Internal hyperlink to a bookmark, keeping ordinary text formatting."""
    paragraph._p.append(parse_xml(
        f'<w:hyperlink {nsdecls("w")} w:anchor="{anchor}" w:history="1">{_run_xml(text)}</w:hyperlink>'))


def rich(paragraph, parts):
    """parts: str | ('b', text) | ('ref', bookmark, shown) | ('pageref', bookmark, shown)
    | ('link', text, anchor) | ('fn', footnote_id)."""
    for part in parts:
        if isinstance(part, str):
            paragraph.add_run(part)
        elif part[0] == "b":
            paragraph.add_run(part[1]).bold = True
        elif part[0] == "ref":
            add_field(paragraph, f"REF {part[1]} \\n \\h", part[2])
        elif part[0] == "pageref":
            add_field(paragraph, f"PAGEREF {part[1]} \\h", part[2])
        elif part[0] == "link":
            add_link(paragraph, part[1], part[2])
        elif part[0] == "fn":
            r = paragraph.add_run()
            r.style = "Footnote Reference"
            r._r.append(parse_xml(f'<w:footnoteReference {nsdecls("w")} w:id="{part[1]}"/>'))
    return paragraph

def make_table(doc, header, rows):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1 + len(rows), cols=len(header))
    t.style = TABLE_STYLE
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    for r_i, row in enumerate([header] + rows):

    return t

def build_numbering(doc):

        '<w:multiLevelType w:val="singleLevel"/>'

        '<w:pStyle w:val="Clause"/><w:lvlText w:val="%1."/><w:lvlJc w:val="left"/>'

def build_footnotes(doc, notes):
    """Create a real footnotes.xml part. notes: {id: text}."""
    W = nsdecls("w")
    sep = ('<w:footnote w:type="{t}" w:id="{i}"><w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="240" '
           'w:lineRule="auto"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:{t}/></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>')
    items = [sep.format(t="separator", i=-1), sep.format(t="continuationSeparator", i=0)]
    for fid, text in notes.items():
        items.append(
            f'<w:footnote w:id="{fid}"><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="FootnoteText"/></w:pPr>'
            '<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="FootnoteReference"/></w:rPr><w:footnoteRef/></w:r>'
            f'<w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">{_esc(text)}</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>')
    xml = ('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n'
           f'<w:footnotes {W}>' + "".join(items) + "</w:footnotes>")
    part = Part(PackURI("/word/footnotes.xml"),
                "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.footnotes+xml",
                xml.encode("utf-8"), doc.part.package)
    doc.part.relate_to(part, RT.FOOTNOTES)

def figure_images():
    """Extract the two figure bitmaps from the issued PDF (Schedule C page)."""
    d = fitz.open(PDF)
    page = d[5]
    infos = sorted(page.get_image_info(xrefs=True), key=lambda i: i["bbox"][1])
    out = []
    for info in infos:

        x0, y0, x1, y1 = info["bbox"]
        out.append((io.BytesIO(img["image"]), (x1 - x0) / 72.0, (y1 - y0) / 72.0))
    return out

# Verification note: agreement.docx reconstruction

## Rebuild
`python /app/submission/rebuild.py` uses python-docx and PyMuPDF to write `agreement.docx` in about 1 s and does not need network access. The script holds the reconstructed text and layout. It takes only the two figure bitmaps from `/app/input/agreement.pdf` at build time. It writes nothing else to `/app/submission`. `/app/input` and `BRIEF.md` were not modified.

## What was checked
- **Text:** I rendered the DOCX with LibreOffice 7.4 and compared the words in order with the source PDF. Both have 1,672 words and there are no differences. All amounts, dates, times, percentages and emails match.
- **Layout:** I compared each page side by side and matched the line baselines numerically. There are 8 pages and each page break falls in the same place as the original. Most lines are within about 1.5 pt of the original; a few are up to about 3 pt off.
  - Page 3 has two columns, starting after a continuous section break.
  - Page 5 (Schedule B) is a landscape section.
  - The header and footer are the same, with a live PAGE field.
- **Structure:**
  - **Styles:** headings use Title, Subtitle, Heading 1 (7) and Heading 2 (19).
  - **Clauses:** clauses 1–8 use one automatic Word numbered list (style "Clause"), which continues across the section breaks.
  - **Tables:** there are 12 real tables in the "Light Shading Accent 1" style. Every header row repeats on a new page and rows can't split across pages. In Schedule A, the Recurring and Summary category cells are vertically merged.
  - **Footnote:** the charge-rules footnote is a real Word footnote (`footnotes.xml`).
  - **Figures:** each figure is an inline picture. Its title is an editable heading with a SEQ Figure field, and its note uses the Caption style.
- **Cross-references:**
  - "clause 8" (in clause 1 and in Execution) is a REF field to a bookmark on clause 8.
  - The page numbers in the cover's Navigation paragraph are PAGEREF fields to bookmarks on each heading.
  - "Appendix E" and "Schedule B" are internal hyperlinks.
- **Editing test:** I lengthened clause 2 and two table cells (Definitions and Schedule B) in a copy and rendered it. The text and table rows reflowed with no overlap or clipping, and it stayed at 8 pages.

## Limitations
- I could only render with LibreOffice; I couldn't check the file in Microsoft Word. Headings use DejaVu Sans and body text uses Liberation Sans, which are the fonts in the source PDF. Where those fonts aren't installed, Word will substitute others and line breaks may change.
- The values shown by the REF and PAGEREF fields are stored in the file. Word shows those stored values until the fields are updated (F9). After clauses are renumbered, the REF field shows the clause's new number.
- The two figures are bitmaps taken from the PDF, so the artwork inside them can't be edited; their captions can.
- Paragraph and table spacing were adjusted by eye to match the PDF. The original style names and XML are not reproduced. In the footnote, the reference number is superscript, where the PDF shows it inline.
